items.name: SUB · Sage Desk brain
items.what: The shared agent brain every channel adapter calls, with inputs channel, user_id and text and outputs reply and handover.
setup: Import this first and note its workflow ID.
Create an OpenAI credential and select it in OpenAI Chat Model; replace YOUR_MODEL with the model you use.
Replace the stand-in agent with Boss 4's agent (tools, guardrails, Check If Evaluating), keeping the same inputs and outputs.
items.test: Click Test workflow: the pinned test input (a wa- user asking about Akobo delivery) should return one item with reply and handover.

items.name: HL · WhatsApp adapter
items.what: Receives WhatsApp messages on the Cloud API test number, ignores receipts, asks for typed text on voice notes or images, and replies through the shared brain.
setup: In Meta for Developers, create an app with the WhatsApp product, add your phone as a verified recipient and send the hello_world template to confirm it arrives.
Create a WhatsApp OAuth credential (Meta app ID and app secret) and select it in WhatsApp Trigger.
Create a WhatsApp API credential with a permanent system user access token and your WhatsApp Business Account ID; select it in Send reply and Please type your message.
Create a Telegram credential and select it in Forward to Tolu.
Replace YOUR_PHONE_NUMBER_ID (twice), YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID and YOUR_BRAIN_WORKFLOW_ID (the ID of SUB · Sage Desk brain).
Publish the workflow on your HTTPS server so Meta registers the production webhook. Test with a separate Meta app, not the live one.
items.test: From your verified phone, send a text to the test number: you get the brain's reply and the brain's execution shows user_id wa-<your number>. Send a voice note: you get the please-type reply and Tolu gets a Telegram. Delivery and read receipts end at Receipt: ignore.

walk.title: Build it: Sage Desk answers on WhatsApp
walk.sample: Iya Basira on WhatsApp · "Do you deliver to Akobo?" · then a voice note · then a read receipt

steps.say: Before n8n, set up Meta. Create an app with the WhatsApp product, add your own phone as a verified recipient, and send the hello world template from the dashboard to prove it reaches you.
show: Meta for Developers › app with WhatsApp

steps.say: Our trigger is the WhatsApp Trigger, listening for messages. Its credential uses your Meta app's ID and secret, and the workflow runs on your HTTPS server.
Meta allows one webhook per app. Testing on the live app replaces the production URL and real customers stop getting through, so publish this one and test with a separate Meta app and number.
Delivery and read receipts arrive on the same webhook as messages. We only pass real text on, or the agent replies twice and even answers delivered.
Now we normalise. The channel prefix on user_id keeps a WhatsApp number from ever mixing with a Telegram chat in memory.
We call the shared brain, Boss 4's agent moved into a sub-workflow. Every channel uses it, so you fix and test it in one place.
show: Workflow: SUB · Sage Desk brain (its ID)
In: channel, user_id, text · Out: reply, handover

steps.say: We reply from our phone number ID to the sender. The customer just wrote, so we're inside the 24-hour window and a free-form reply is allowed and free.
Its credential is the WhatsApp API one: business account ID and a permanent system user token. The dashboard's temporary token expires, and every send fails the next morning.
On the false side we split again. If there's a sender, it's a customer who sent a voice note or picture. If not, it's only a receipt.
A voice note gets a polite reply asking them to type, so the brain never wastes a call on something it can't read.
show: Text: Please type your message so we can help…

steps.say: And Tolu gets a Telegram, so a customer who can't type is still seen by a person.
Receipts end here, doing nothing. Point your Telegram adapter at the same brain with tg- user IDs, and both channels share one set of tools and guardrails.
One rule this adapter doesn't need, but your order updates do: after 24 hours since the customer's last message, only an approved template like order_ready can go, and only to customers who opted in.

walk.end: Text from your verified phone, then send a voice note: one brain reply, one please-type message, a Telegram for Tolu, and the receipts quietly ignored.

items.name: HL · Telegram adapter
items.what: Points the existing Telegram bot at the same shared brain with tg- user IDs.
setup: Create a Telegram credential with your bot token and select it in the trigger and both Telegram send nodes.
Replace YOUR_BRAIN_WORKFLOW_ID with the ID of SUB · Sage Desk brain.
Turn off your old Telegram bot workflow so only one listens to the bot.
items.test: Message your bot: it answers as before, and the brain's execution shows user_id tg-<chat id>.

items.name: HL · Order dispatched WhatsApp update
items.what: Sends an order-dispatched update only to opted-in customers: free-form inside the 24-hour window, the approved utility template order_ready outside it, and logs which path ran.
setup: In WhatsApp Manager, create the utility template order_ready with three body variables (name, order number, arrival time) and wait for approval.
Select your WhatsApp API credential in Free-form update, and in Send Template order_ready (HTTP Request, Authentication: Predefined credential type, WhatsApp API).
Create a Google Sheets credential and select it in Window log.
Replace YOUR_PHONE_NUMBER_ID (twice) and YOUR_SHEET_ID; add a tab Window log with columns order_id, phone, path, template_name, category, sent_at.
In Dispatched order (test data), put your own verified phone number in phone instead of +2348000000000. Check the template language code matches the one you submitted.
items.test: Run it as is (last message 30 hours ago): the template path runs and Window log shows order_ready / utility. Change last_customer_msg_at to an expression of 2 hours ago and run again: the free-form path runs. Set opted_in to false: nothing is sent.
